title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X' is a small category. Y' ⊂ X' is a 'closed' full subcategory with 'open' complement U'. Arrows only go from U' to Y' (the page uses Hom(u',y') with u' ∈ U', y' ∈ Y'). In standard terms Y' is a cosieve and U' a sieve, so Grothendieck is using the Alexandrov-type topology on Cat with open = sieve. A functor f : X → X' is given, with Y = f^{-1}(Y') and U = f^{-1}(U'). This produces two squares: Y ↪ X ↩ U over Y' ↪ X' ↩ U'. Y is again a cosieve in X.

Question. Assume U → U' is an isomorphism. Is the square (Y → X, Y → Y', Y' → X') necessarily cocartesian in Cat, i.e. is X' = X ⊔_Y Y'?

First answer: no. Take X = U' with f the inclusion. Then Y = ∅, and the pushout is the disjoint union U' ⊔ Y', which loses the arrows from U' to Y'.

Second question: what if f is cofibred (an opfibration)? Objects of X ⊔_Y Y' are Ob U ⊔ Ob Y' ≅ Ob X'. Since Y is a cosieve, the only new morphisms are from u to y'. They are classes of pairs (u → y in X, g(y) → y' in Y'), so Hom(u, y') = colim over the comma category Y/y' of Hom_X(u, y). Cocartesianness therefore amounts to the canonical map colim_{Y/y'} Hom_X(u, y) → Hom_{X'}(u', y') being bijective.

Grothendieck answers yes.
(i) Surjectivity: any φ : u' → y' lifts to a cocartesian arrow u → φ_!(u), which lies in the fibre Y_{y'}.
(ii) Injectivity: for fixed φ, the category of factorisations u → y → y' lying over φ has an initial object, the cocartesian lift. So it is connected, and the colimit identifies all its elements.

Conclusion of the page. He restricts attention to such squares: f cofibred with trivial fibres over U'. Up to equivalence these are the same as functors X' → Cat whose restriction to U' is constant with value the point e = Δ_0. Such a functor amounts to two pieces of data:
(i) a functor Φ : Y' → Cat, which gives Y → Y' by the Grothendieck construction;
(ii) a map Hom(u', y') → Ob Φ(y'), natural (a 'bifunctor') in (u', y') ∈ U'^op × Y'.
So this is a gluing ('recollement') description of cofibred categories over a sieve/cosieve decomposition.

Purpose. The next page uses this to ask whether the comparison map ∫(i, g) → X' = X ⊔_Y Y' lies in W, i.e. is aspherical. He wants the strict pushout to be a homotopy pushout. He then observes that the comparison map is cofibred with fibres that are points over U' and cone-like categories C(Y_{y'}) with a final object over Y'. This is part of his 1983 programme on the 'cohomological properties of maps in (Cat)': base change and asphericity for basic localizers W.
errors: No real error. Two minor gaps. First, the passage from cofibred categories to functors X' → Cat holds only up to equivalence: in general one gets pseudofunctors, so one must use a normalised cleavage or replace the data by a strict functor. Second, the injectivity argument is only sketched ('pour f : u → y' fixé ...'). It is correct: the category of factorisations of a fixed arrow through the fibre has an initial object, the cocartesian lift.
The counterexample X = U', Y = ∅ only works when Hom_{X'}(U', Y') is nonempty. This is tacit but harmless.

ideas.what: Open/closed decomposition of a small category: a sieve U' with complementary cosieve Y', all arrows going U' → Y', so that X' is recovered from U', Y' and the profunctor Hom(U', Y').
ideas.modern_name: Sieve/cosieve decomposition; X' as the collage (cograph) of a profunctor; Alexandrov topology on Cat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; open/closed (sieve/cosieve) language in Grothendieck's homotopy theory of Cat is expounded by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs use sieves and cosieves (cribles, cocribles) extensively; the exact open/closed phrasing here is unsure

ideas.what: Criterion: if f is cofibred and an isomorphism over the open part U', then the square along the closed cosieve Y' is cocartesian in Cat, i.e. X' = X ⊔_Y Y'.
ideas.modern_name: Pushouts along cosieves in Cat; computation of Hom-sets in a pushout of categories along a (co)sieve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related structural work on pushouts along Dwyer maps by Thomason (1980) and Cisinski

ideas.what: Cofibred categories over X' that are trivial over U' are equivalent to gluing data: Φ : Y' → Cat plus a natural map Hom(u', y') → Ob Φ(y').
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck construction combined with recollement / gluing along a profunctor (lax-limit description of Cat-valued functors on a collage)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck construction (SGA1); gluing description is folklore

ideas.what: Aim (realised on the next page): such strict pushouts are homotopy pushouts. The comparison ∫(i, g) → X' is cofibred with aspherical fibres, so it lies in W and does so universally (stable under base change).
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy cocartesian squares in Cat for basic localizers; Thomason's homotopy-colimit theorem; Quillen's Theorem A for opfibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1979/1980), Cisinski (Les préfaisceaux comme modèles des types d'homotopie, 2006), Maltsiniotis (2005)
ideas.where_published: Related asphericity and base-change criteria appear in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; this specific statement is unsure

missed.claim: This is an explicit 1983 derivation of a criterion for strict pushouts in Cat along a cosieve to be cocartesian (f cofibred and an isomorphism over the open complement), with a gluing classification of such squares. It is the first step toward showing these pushouts are W-homotopy pushouts for any basic localizer. This parallels later work on Dwyer maps and Thomason cofibrations (Cisinski, Bruckner–Pegel), but uses an opfibration hypothesis instead of the Dwyer hypothesis. The result is essentially known or folklore; at most it is unrecorded as Grothendieck's.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents Grothendieck working on homotopy-pushout criteria in Cat for arbitrary basic localizers. This is a variant of the Dwyer-map condition expressed through opfibrations, which is not the form usually cited.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, fairly routine category theory (Hom-sets in pushouts along cosieves; Grothendieck construction as gluing data). It serves a homotopy-pushout question whose answers are by now known through Thomason/Cisinski-type results. Only mildly interesting as an unpublished record of Grothendieck's 1983 Cat-homotopy programme.
transcription_corrections: '[-Mimi-][?]' at top right is not part of the mathematics; it appears to be faint bleed-through or a stray word and should be dropped.
'cofibrant' here means cofibred (opfibration), not cofibrant in the model-category sense.

The second colimit line is probably '≅ lim_{Y_{y'}} Hom(u, y)' or 'lim_{Y/y'} Hom(u, Y_{y'})', i.e. a reduction of the colimit over the comma category Y/y' to one over the fibre Y_{y'}; the subscript is the fibre Y_{y'}.
'(où u ∈ Ob U au-dessus de u')' is correct: u is the unique object of U over u'.
'avec f cocartésien' should read 'avec le carré cocartésien' or 'f cofibrant'. The underlined word 'cocartésien' qualifies the diagrams of the previous type.
'définissant f : Y → Y'' should read 'définissant g : Y → Y''; the f is struck out.
In the small diagram, the dashed arrow u' ⇢ y' is labelled with a struck-out 'f' or 'φ'.
